title: Retail Installment Contracts Payoff Statement Terms: Figure, Statement Interest and Good-Through Date
content:
**1. The statement.** A payoff statement on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts quotes the principal balance plus fees due plus statement interest through its good-through date, rounded half-up to the cent, and its good-through date is the quote date plus the product's payoff quote validity in calendar days.

**2. Statement interest.** Statement interest is simple interest at the contract's APR on the principal balance on an actual/365 basis for the calendar days from the latest posted payment — the payment with the latest posting date, and among payments of the same date the one recorded first — or from the contract date when none has posted, to the good-through date, the new interest rounded half-up to the cent, plus the unpaid interest carried. When that latest posted payment was itself returned, the interest portion its return reversed is counted in place of the unpaid interest carried.

**3. Assembly.** The number of days can be replaced, days can be added to it or taken from it, and an amount can be added to the figure; the good-through date is then the quote date plus the resulting days, never earlier than the quote date, and the statement figure is the principal balance plus fees due plus statement interest through that good-through date plus every amount added, rounded half-up to the cent.

| Part of the figure | Taken from |
|---|---|
| principal balance | the contract's principal balance on the quote date |
| fees due | the contract's fees due on the quote date |
| statement interest | clause 2, through the good-through date |
| carried interest | the unpaid interest carried, or the interest portion reversed by the return of the latest posted payment when that payment was returned |

## Worked figures (hypothetical contract)

Principal 6400.00 at 19.90%; fees due 25.00; unpaid interest carried 0.00; latest posted payment 40 days before the quote date, not returned; a validity of 10 days.

- Good-through date: quote date plus 10 days, so the interest runs 40 plus 10, that is 50 days.
- New interest: 6400.00 multiplied by 19.90% by 50, divided by 365, that is 174.465…, rounded to 174.47.
- Figure: 6400.00 plus 25.00 plus 174.47, that is 6599.47.

Had that latest payment been returned, with its return reversing 61.20 of interest, the carried part would be 61.20 and the figure 6660.67.
